name: Kensuke Naito
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of SmartHR (Japanese cloud HR/labor-management SaaS, launched 2015, valued ~$2B). SmartHR's own site and press credit Shoji Miyata as founder; current CEO is ex-CTO Masato Serizawa. Naito's specific role could not be verified from a primary source in this session.
interesting_fact: SmartHR was inspired by founder Shoji Miyata's personal experience dealing with paperwork; the service launched in 2015 and is used by tens of thousands of Japanese companies.
notes: Only CB Insights lists Naito as founder; SmartHR's official pages name Shoji Miyata. Could not confirm Naito's role or whether he is still at the company; verify before outreach (likely route via SmartHR corporate PR).

name: Sudheer Koneru
profile: IIT Madras and UT Austin computer-science grad who spent ~8 years at Microsoft, then ran e-learning firm Intelliprep (merged into Click2learn/SumTotal Systems). After co-founding a spa/fitness chain in Hyderabad, he founded Zenoti (originally ManageMySpa) in 2010; it became the beauty-and-wellness software industry's first unicorn and powers 30,000+ businesses.
interesting_fact: Zenoti grew out of his own pain running Latitudes Health Club and Tangerine Spas, a fitness/spa/salon chain he co-founded with his brother Dheeraj in Hyderabad in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: He practices yoga, tracks workouts with the Nike+ app, names Ubud in Bali as a favorite place, and says his life mantra is 'Live and be present to the moment'; he credits his father's habit of focusing on the points he missed on tests for how he coaches employees.
notes: No published press email found on Zenoti's press/contact pages; use the press page or contact form.

name: Li Zhan
current_role: Founder & CEO, Tungee (探迹科技), Guangzhou
profile: Li Zhan (黎展) is a serial entrepreneur who studied software engineering and business administration at Sun Yat-sen University and worked on personalized-recommendation research in Tencent's cloud platform division. He founded Tungee in Guangzhou in 2016; it sells AI-driven B2B sales software (lead mining, outreach, CRM) and raised from backers including Sequoia China and Qiming.
interesting_fact: Tungee's sales search engine claims coverage of 300M+ Chinese market entities, 9M+ factories and 300M+ tender notices, and now markets a 'Sales Agent' AI product.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tungee he was CEO of an earlier startup, Jiaxue (佳学); he placed second nationally in the Microsoft Elite Challenge, was a Microsoft outstanding MSP (student partner), and was the youngest member of the Great Wall Club.
notes: No published press email; company site lists only a sales hotline and a recruitment email. Chinese-language outreach likely best; WeChat official account is the main company channel.

name: Matt Fuller
current_role: Co-founder; Vice President, AI/ML Products and board member, Starburst
profile: Database engineer who was an early Vertica engineer, then a principal engineer at SQL-on-Hadoop startup Hadapt, which Teradata acquired in 2014; at Teradata he led Presto (now Trino) engineering in Boston. That team spun out as Starburst in 2017, the commercial Trino/lakehouse company; Fuller remains on its board and leads AI/ML products.
interesting_fact: He co-authored O'Reilly's 'Trino: The Definitive Guide' with Trino co-creator Martin Traverso and Manfred Moser.
deep_cut_fact: He says he got into databases via the C-Store research paper, which led him to join Vertica (the columnar database that grew out of it), where he co-built the query optimizer.
notes: Engineer-founder, low public profile; CEO Justin Borgman is the main public face. Vertica optimizer detail is from Strata speaker bio/Crunchbase summary in search; C-Store origin from podcast notes.

name: Blake Scholl
profile: Cincinnati-born Carnegie Mellon computer scientist who worked at early Amazon, then co-founded mobile startup Kima Labs (acquired by Groupon in 2012). He founded Boom in 2014 to build the Overture supersonic airliner; its XB-1 demonstrator went supersonic in 2025. In Dec 2025 Boom launched 'Superpower', a 42 MW natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, with a 1.21 GW launch order from Crusoe plus a $300M raise.
interesting_fact: Boom's Superpower turbine shares the core of its Symphony jet engine, needs no water, and Crusoe ordered 29 units (1.21 GW, >$1.25B backlog); Scholl says turbine revenue will help fund Overture. Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He left high school early on a scholarship for early entry to Carnegie Mellon, earned his private pilot license in 2007, and before founding Boom took aircraft-design classes and built his own aerodynamics model in early 2014; he put half his Kima sale proceeds into Boom.
notes: Very media-friendly and active on X (company account x.com/boomsupersonic linked from Boom site; personal handle not verified this session). Data-center power pivot makes him a strong podcast fit.

name: Eric Chen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Injective Labs (also leads the Injective Foundation)
profile: Chinese-American entrepreneur (b. 1998) who studied business and computer science at NYU, was involved with NYU's blockchain lab, then took leave in 2018 to co-found Injective with Albert Chon. Injective, incubated by Binance Labs, is a finance-focused Layer-1 blockchain backed by Pantera, Jump Crypto and Mark Cuban; he was on Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance (2024).
interesting_fact: Injective received $500,000 from Binance Labs' first incubation program in 2018, later raising from Pantera (2020), a token sale including Mark Cuban (2021) and a $40M round led by Jump Crypto (2022).
deep_cut_fact: In 2026 he co-authored a peer-reviewed paper in the journal Mathematics (MDPI) simulating an EIP-1559-style dynamic fee market for Injective's 600 ms blocks, finding proper tuning cut peak fees by 31% under variable demand.
notes: Common name - confirm it's the Injective CEO. Frequent podcast guest (CryptoNews Podcast, CNBC Crypto World). institutions@ is Injective's institutional inquiry address, not press. Wikipedia article flagged for source reliability.

name: Oliver Dlugosch
current_role: Co-founder & CCO, GeneralMind (Berlin AI supply-chain startup); co-founder of Razor Group
profile: Dr. Oliver Dlugosch trained as a physicist, moved into consulting and operating roles, and in 2020 co-founded Berlin e-commerce aggregator Razor Group (COO), which acquired and integrated 300+ Amazon/e-commerce brands. In 2025 the Razor founding team launched GeneralMind, an 'AI system of action' that automates email/spreadsheet-heavy supply-chain operations; it raised $12M in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: GeneralMind's $12M round was led by Lakestar, Leo Capital and others; the startup is based in Berlin with a second site in Bangalore.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in physics, not e-commerce; he says he joined Razor in 2020 after his schoolmate Tushar Ahluwalia pitched him the idea.
notes: Now focused on GeneralMind rather than Razor. Appeared on the 'Behind the Click' podcast (E-commerce Germany, Sept 2026). Company emails are general inboxes (hello@/info@).

name: James Alexander
current_role: Director, Future Agenda (foresight/strategy think tank); co-founder of Zopa
profile: Former LEK consultant (worked on Co-operative Bank's online bank Smile) and Egg strategy director who co-founded Zopa in 2005, the world's first peer-to-peer lender, later serving as its CEO and a board director before leaving. He now advises boards on foresight, strategy and innovation via Future Agenda, chairs Environmental Finance and advises fintechs such as Seedrs and LandBay.
interesting_fact: He was awarded an MBE for services to the environment.
deep_cut_fact: He is a former trustee of the RSPB and Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and launched the #voicefortheplanet environmental movement at the World Economic Forum in 2019; he also helped with dothegreenthing.org.
notes: No longer operational at Zopa. Published Future Agenda work email is the best direct route; also bookable as a speaker via Speaker Solutions. Strong environment/climate angle.

name: Karsten Temme
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
profile: Bioengineer (Iowa BS/MS; UC Berkeley-UCSF PhD) who in Chris Voigt's lab tried to rebuild microbial nitrogen fixation from scratch. In 2011 he co-founded Pivot Bio with Alvin Tamsir to replace synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with nitrogen-fixing soil microbes, serving as CEO until 2023; he now leads innovation focused on 'the Future Acre' (agriculture in 2050).
interesting_fact: He holds over 200 patents or patent applications (90+ granted) and spoke at the TED Countdown Summit in Nairobi in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Originally from Casper, Wyoming, he played trumpet in the University of Iowa's Hawkeye Marching Band, helped design parts for a Mars rover, and as an undergrad founded Xwires Communications to bring internet service to remote farmland.
notes: Chris Abbott replaced him as CEO in Aug 2023. Experienced TED speaker; climate/ag-emissions angle (synthetic fertilizer is energy-intensive).

name: Daniela Espinosa
current_role: Founder, Crakit (tech advisory & M&A boutique); co-founder, UIN; angel investor
profile: Ecuadorian banker-turned-founder: 12 years at Citibank (ending as Country Risk Manager for Ecuador), then CFO of large family-owned groups, before co-founding payments platform Kushki in 2016, which became Ecuador's first unicorn. She left Kushki in 2022, founded advisory firm Crakit in 2023 and co-founded UIN (gamification + AI for consumer behaviour) in 2025, while angel investing and advising fintechs.
interesting_fact: She was president of Ecuador's Technology and Innovation Chamber (CITEC) and helped build Kushki, whose payment rails have served clients such as Uber, Cabify and Rappi.
deep_cut_fact: As a child she loved numbers so much she memorized license plates and phone numbers, and her favourite game was Monopoly; she became a Citi country manager by age 29.
notes: No longer at Kushki (2016-2022). No published email or verified own website found; LinkedIn (ec.linkedin.com/in/daespinosa) appears in search but was not verified as hers. Speaks at South Summit Madrid; Spanish-language outreach likely best.
